solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enchant? Church might

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
might or power, as in the long arm of the law

explanation.surface: A question about whether a church could cast a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: 'Enchant?' is the definition, and 'Church might' reads like an answer to it but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to charm and to enchant both originally meant casting a spell, and both now mean delighting someone.

clue.text: Disgusted by repeated fine after Lancashire possibly cheat

indicators.note: something repeated appears twice, so fine's F is written two times
what comes after is placed later in the answer

parts.note: Lancashire is a type of English cheese; 'possibly' marks it as an example
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: Someone upset by a Lancashire cheat who keeps getting fined.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire reads as the English county but is the crumbly cheese named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal idiom: cheesed off means fed up or annoyed, close enough to disgusted in the sense of exasperated.

clue.text: Affirmed removing leader's support

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone who stated they backed a leader now withdrawing that support.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: aid, as a noun, is help or support given to someone.

clue.text: Intend to capture marine creature not truly of the sea

definitions.text: creature not truly of the sea

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it

explanation.surface: Someone planning to catch a sea creature that doesn't really belong to the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine creature' looks like one phrase but splits: marine is RM, creature starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a merman lives in the sea only in legend, so it is a creature not truly of the sea because it is not real.

clue.text: Poor works in dodgy sci-fi causing one to crash

indicators.note: to work something is to shape or knead it, so POOR is reshaped
one thing in another sits inside it, so the reshaped POOR goes inside the other
dodgy means unreliable, so SCIFI's letters cannot be trusted to stay put

explanation.surface: A review of bad science fiction that sends viewers to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Crash here is slang for falling asleep, not a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: to crash is to fall fast asleep, and something soporific induces sleep.

clue.text: Guarantee bit of pork trimmed by butcher showing skill with blade

indicators.note: a trim runs round the edge of a garment

parts.note: to give your word is to guarantee

explanation.surface: A butcher proving deft with a knife by trimming pork.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets up a butcher's knife, and the definition is about blades too, but it means fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: Swordplay is fencing or sword fighting, the art of handling a blade well.

clue.text: Theatrical work, elevated work about soldier

indicators.note: raised up; in a down clue that means read from bottom to top

parts.note: OP (opus, a work), written upwards as PO

explanation.surface: A description of a lofty play about a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'work' twice: once inside the definition, once as OP. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick and audience shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Panto is the informal short form of pantomime, a kind of theatrical production.

clue.text: Danger: IT could become a significant part of our universe

definitions.text: a significant part of our universe

indicators.note: letters that could become something else are turned into a new word by rearranging

explanation.surface: A warning that information technology might take over the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: IT in capitals looks like information technology but is simply two letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a red giant is a huge ageing star, and stars are a sizeable part of the universe.

clue.text: Imminent and taking shape, involving most of the firm

indicators.note: to involve is to include within
most of a word is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: A company plan about to materialise, with most of the firm involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' applies only to 'the', not to the whole firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: forthcoming describes what is about to appear or happen, which is what imminent means.

clue.text: Pitch marker clubs abandoned abruptly

indicators.note: something ended abruptly is cut short

explanation.surface: A golf pitch where the clubs were left behind in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch and clubs suggest sport; the pitch is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a stave that fixes the pitch of the notes, so it marks pitch.

clue.text: Cover, scarlet, that is turned over blue

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped end to end

explanation.surface: A red bedspread flipped over to show a blue side.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue reads as a colour beside scarlet, but it means low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt stuffed with duck down, a bed cover.

clue.text: Lament opening of electricity network being put back

indicators.note: put back means sent backwards

parts.note: the electricity grid is a network

explanation.surface: Grief over the power grid's launch being postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as delayed but tells you to reverse EGRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dirge is a mournful song for the dead, a lament.

clue.text: Tongue, European tongue, coming about with formality

parts.note: a spit is a tongue of land

explanation.surface: Two languages being spoken on a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Both tongues suggest languages, but the first is a spit, a narrow tongue of land jutting into water.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from military boot-cleaning: spit and polish means great attention to smart appearance and ceremony, i.e. formality.

clue.text: Mischief over US city blues I played? Unlikely

indicators.note: notes played are performed in a new arrangement, so BLUESI is rearranged
in a down clue one thing over another sits above it

parts.note: a mischief is a naughty child, an imp

explanation.surface: A musician doubting they played the blues in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Mischief is used in its concrete sense, a mischievous child, rather than the behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: implausible means not easy to believe, hence unlikely.

clue.text: Allegedly and conceivably dropping No 1, retaining rest of soccer team?

indicators.note: the number one letter is the first, and dropping it leaves OSSIBLY

parts.note: possibly = conceivably; minus its first letter
a soccer side is eleven; take away one and ten remain

explanation.surface: A report on a football team with its first-choice player dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: No 1 hints at the goalkeeper's shirt but instructs removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ostensibly means apparently, as stated, which is what allegedly conveys.

clue.text: Fool expected to seize power

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold

explanation.surface: An idiot who is predicted to take control.
explanation.walkthrough: Fool reads as a noun but works equally as a verb; dupe is both.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to dupe is to trick, and a dupe is a person tricked, a fool.

clue.text: Those opposing going round hobbling birds

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it

explanation.surface: Enemies circling and injuring birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Flamingoes famously stand on one leg, which makes 'hobbling birds' a neat touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: flamingoes are pink wading birds.

clue.text: Lecture, perhaps, has Mike working with introduction, extracting press release

indicators.note: to extract is to pull out

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A talk that a man called Mike gives with an introduction but no press release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the lecture as one example of a monologue.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a lecture is one speaker talking at length, a kind of monologue.

clue.text: A drinking challenge knocking out one European in Welsh town

indicators.note: to knock out is to remove

parts.note: E = European; one of BEER's two Es goes

explanation.surface: A drinking dare in Wales that ends with a foreign visitor knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdare is a town in the South Wales valleys; the Welsh setting fits the drinking-game surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdare is a real town in the Cynon Valley in south Wales.

clue.text: Gorgeously-coloured insects surrounding a doctor heading for Oaxaca

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose

parts.note: two insects: fly and ant, split FL…YANT

explanation.surface: Brightly coloured Mexican insects swarming around a doctor bound for Oaxaca.
explanation.walkthrough: Oaxaca is a Mexican state; only its O is used. The flamboyant is also a tropical tree with vivid red flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant describes something showy and vivid, and is especially used of brilliant colours.

clue.text: I have to follow source of Government grant

indicators.note: to follow is to come after

explanation.surface: Someone awaiting a government grant.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant reads as a noun beside Government but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to grant something is to give it formally.

clue.text: Tried out adopting old computer program

indicators.note: out means not in its proper state, so TRIED is disordered

explanation.surface: Testing some old computer software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried out' reads as tested, but out is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a text editor is a program for writing and changing files.

clue.text: What indicates senior officer took off immediately with bombs?

parts.note: fighter pilots scramble, taking off at once

explanation.surface: Fighter planes launching in a hurry carrying bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds abstract but refers to a uniform detail; the wordplay is all air-force slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Service slang: scrambled eggs is the gold braid on the peak of a senior officer's cap, which marks rank.

clue.text: Staff sell fruit

explanation.surface: Shop workers selling fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff reads as a noun for workers, but it is the verb: to man a stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the mango is a tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Pressure off agreements in items of legislation

indicators.note: something off is detached

parts.note: pacts are agreements; drop the P

explanation.surface: Pressure easing during treaty negotiations over new laws.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue starts with the letter to remove, before the word it comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws passed by a parliament are called Acts, each one an item of legislation.

clue.text: Emergency committee's support led by army chief

indicators.note: whatever leads goes in front

parts.note: a bra is a support garment

explanation.surface: An emergency committee getting backing from the head of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name: COBRA is the UK government's crisis committee, named after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A.

clue.text: Entertainment venue near Bath opened by 10cc

parts.note: 10 cubic centimetres is one centilitre, cl

explanation.surface: A music venue near the city of Bath launched by the rock band 10cc.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is the English city and 10cc a 1970s band, but here bath is a tub and 10cc is a measure: one centilitre.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a nightclub is a place for late drinking, music and dancing.

clue.text: Disrespect I found in recording

indicators.note: something found in another is located inside it

explanation.surface: Someone discovering they were insulted on a tape.
explanation.walkthrough: Recording suggests a tape or video; the crossword standard is LP, a vinyl album.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: lip is cheeky, insolent talk, as in 'don't give me any lip'.

clue.text: Dockworker set aside nets day by day

indicators.note: to net something is to catch it

parts.note: to store is to set aside
an eve is the day before

explanation.surface: A docker putting away nets every single day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nets' reads as fishing gear on a dock but is a verb meaning catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stevedore loads and unloads ships at the docks.

clue.text: Respond, taking answer from second view

indicators.note: taking something away removes it, so A comes out

parts.note: a replay lets you view something a second time

explanation.surface: Someone reacting after watching something again.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits definition from wordplay; 'answer' is the single letter A, not the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to reply is to answer, to make a response.
